summary: Iteration 101 — Catalog integrity (user's reported bug) + Etsy governance gating after imprint migration & activate-pipeline extension. 15 pytest cases + Playwright UI validation on /etsy. Catalog is COMPLETE: exactly 8 authorized books, imprints canonicalized to {E.Q. Rothwell™, QRU Press™}, 'Patterns of Intelligence' (BOOK-0013) exists under E.Q. Rothwell™, BOOK-0003 duplicate is gone, BOOK-0004 canonical Ordinary Tuesdays intact. Security + no-secret-leak + publish approval/disconnected gates all pass. Found 1 real bug (KeyError on preview) and 1 governance-ordering deviation on activate.

minor.issue: Governance-order deviation: when NO mapping exists, activate() returns 'No Etsy draft is mapped...' even when approved=false — but the review spec requires 'with {approved:false} on any state returns requires_approval=true'. The approval gate should run BEFORE the mapping check to match the stated contract. Currently order is: mapping → already-active → approval → uploads.

ui_bugs.issue: Clicking Preview returned HTTP 500 and 'Preview failed' toast. Root cause: etsy_integration.preview() read payload['taxonomy_id'] unconditionally, but _listing_payload() only sets that key when a taxonomy is configured (env var missing in preview). Fixed inline with .get('taxonomy_id') — panel now opens correctly with no toast.
ui_bugs.priority: HIGH (was blocking preview for every book)

action_items: Reorder governance gates in etsy_integration.activate_listing() so that when approved=false the API returns {requires_approval:true} regardless of mapping state (spec: 'with {approved:false} on any state returns requires_approval=true'). Move the `if not approved` check to the top of the function.
Verify the taxonomy_id fix (.get instead of []) I applied in etsy_integration.preview() line 696 — trivial and safe, but please code-review.
critical_code_review_comments: etsy_integration.py line 696 assumed payload['taxonomy_id'] exists but _listing_payload only sets it when DEFAULT_TAXONOMY_ID or explicit taxonomy_id is provided. Under normal preview-env (no env var) every call to POST /products/{id}/preview 500s. Fixed to .get(). Add a unit test that runs preview() with DEFAULT_TAXONOMY_ID unset to prevent regression.

activate_listing() gate ordering doesn't match the review-request contract (approval-first). Small but visible: the API 'leaks' the internal mapping state before enforcing Founder approval. Consider a canonical gate order: approval → connected → mapping → uploads → already-active.

publish_draft() and activate_listing() are shape-mixed (200 with {error} body vs raising). Consistent: return non-200 for hard errors, keep 200 only for {ok:true} and {requires_approval:true}. (Not fixed — behavior change.)
eligibility() detail strings are still opaque; e.g., 'Metadata populated' failing doesn't say which field. Nice-to-have from prior iteration remains open.

success_rate.backend: 93% (14/15 pytest; the 1 failure is the activate gate-order deviation described above)

rca of the issue.user_reported_bug_catalog_integrity: NOT A BUG — catalog is complete. All 8 authorized book_codes present, Patterns of Intelligence (BOOK-0013) exists and is E.Q. Rothwell™-imprinted, BOOK-0003 is the only trashed record. Publishing may proceed on catalog grounds.
rca of the issue.found_bug_preview_500: etsy_integration.preview() referenced payload['taxonomy_id'] with subscript access; _listing_payload only sets that key when DEFAULT_TAXONOMY_ID env or explicit tid arg is present. In preview env neither is set → KeyError → 500 → UI toast 'Preview failed'. Reproduction: POST /api/integrations/etsy/products/BOOK-0001/preview as super-admin. Mitigation: use payload.get('taxonomy_id') (applied).
